A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ReWind research work and complete supplementary material. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison despite supplementary renumbering and unresolved citation markers in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original ReWind results for video question answering, temporal grounding, component ablations, memory consumption, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds zero-shot ReWind evaluations on MSRVTT-QA and MSVD-QA.

M1.justification: The read-perceive-write memory, instruction-conditioned perceiver, dynamic frame selection, LLM inputs, SigLIP pretraining, and LoRA instruction tuning remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds MSRVTT-QA and MSVD-QA evaluation alongside the retained MovieChat-1K, Charades-STA, and VideoChatGPT tests. This extends the existing short-video VQA coverage without changing training datasets or introducing another task.

E2.justification: MA-LMM, previously discussed only as related work, becomes a numerical comparator in supplementary Table 1, with accuracies of 48.5 on MSRVTT-QA and 60.6 on MSVD-QA. Existing comparisons retain their baselines. VTimeLLM's all-dash row in the new table supplies no additional evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: The added short-video experiments specify zero-shot evaluation with GPT-3.5 accuracy and score reporting, alongside the retained VideoChatGPT generation-quality evaluation. Existing experimental settings, metrics, and training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 4-9, Figure 4, and the qualitative examples retain the same component, conditioning, frame-count, token-count, and frame-selection analyses. The new supplementary table adds benchmark scores without introducing an ablation or diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results follow the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Supplementary Table 1 adds ReWind accuracy/score results of 56.9/3.4 on MSRVTT-QA and 69.3/3.8 on MSVD-QA. ReWind leads MSRVTT-QA score and ties MovieChat on MSVD-QA score; accuracy leaders are LLaMA-VID at 58.3 and MovieChat at 75.2, respectively. All matched original results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.3's clustering definitions, density and distance-index equations, and associated mathematical reasoning are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient long-video understanding, temporal fidelity, instructed memory, and adaptive frame selection. The new benchmarks support the existing short-video applicability claim.

C2.justification: The explanations of temporal coherence, instruction guidance, degradation with excessive frames, memory requirements, and hallucinations remain substantively unchanged. The new short-video summary reinforces an existing interpretation without adding a mechanism explanation or limitation.

D1.justification: The new supplementary comparison specifies the added MA-LMM comparator's Vicuna-7B LLM and ViT-G backbone. ReWind's training hyperparameters, hardware, frame processing, and pretrained-model access links are retained.

R1.justification: The BERT paper listed as reference 7 in v1 is absent from v2's bibliography, although BERT remains used and named. Otherwise, the related-work discussion and research positioning are unchanged; most citation-number differences are renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgments and a leading supplementary experiments section, changes appendix headings A-D to sections 2-5, and shortens some ablation and qualitative prose. The main narrative remains intact. Supplementary citations now appear as unresolved question marks.

P2.justification: v2 adds supplementary Table 1 and reflows the supplement. Existing Table 10 and Figures 6-8 remain as supplementary Table 2 and Figures 1-3. Other displays are retained with limited caption/layout edits. The new table's caption incorrectly includes VideoChatGPT despite showing only MSRVTT-QA and MSVD-QA columns.

improvement.justification: The added zero-shot benchmarks strengthen evidence for short-video generalization beyond v1's VideoChatGPT evaluation. This provides a limited empirical improvement while preserving the original method and results. Unresolved supplementary citations and the inaccurate new table caption reduce traceability and polish, tempering the benefit.
